result:
I'd make changing your mind feel like relief instead of humiliation.

So much of what goes wrong in the world persists not because nobody knows better, but because backing down costs too much. Wars drag on because leaders can't admit the war was a mistake, bad policies outlive the evidence against them, and family feuds run for decades over things neither side still believes. Being wrong feels like a small death, so people defend positions long after they've stopped holding them.

If being wrong felt the way it feels to put down something heavy, I think a lot of other problems would start solving themselves. Arguments would become searches instead of battles, and science would move faster. Apologies would come easier.

I considered bigger wishes, like ending disease or poverty. But I trust this one more because it doesn't require me to be right about what the world needs. It just makes everyone better at figuring that out and correcting course, including correcting whatever I'd have gotten wrong with a bigger wish.

What would yours be?
